Cover prints 488 new samples analysed and 72 positive (14.8%; 72/488 = 14.8%). 72 equals the 72 new cases. 488 equals the counts received or analysed in Nord-Kivu (165 received), Ituri (264 received and tested), Haut-Uele (30 analysed), Bas-Uele (7 received), Nord-Ubangi (12 received) and Tshopo (10 received); it includes 1 Nord-Kivu sample in progress, 1 non-conforming Bas-Uele sample and 8 Nord-Ubangi samples awaiting analysis, and the printed analysed counts sum to 468 plus an unstated Tshopo count. Nord-Kivu care prints 521 patients (108 confirmed, 413 suspects): 312 in CTE/CT on 434 beds (72%; 103 of 203 confirmed beds and 209 of 231 suspect beds) and 209 in health facilities outside CTE/CT (5 confirmed, 204 suspects), which all reconcile; 98 admissions (4 confirmed, 94 suspects) and 85 exits (17 recovered, 55 non-cases, 13 deaths of which 10 confirmed). No carry-over is printed; the SR185 end-of-day 514 with these flows gives 527, not 521, and the confirmed split does not close either (SR185 125 confirmed + 4 confirmed admissions - 17 recovered - 10 confirmed deaths = 102, against 108 printed). The census is kept as printed, the 72% is kept only as the rate for the 312 patients in CTE/CT, and the SR185 figure is not changed.

Ituri care prints 394 patients (139 confirmed, 255 suspects) with a global occupancy of 37% (24% confirmed, 49% suspects); the printed patients and the two rates give 35.3% to 36.4%, so the 37% is withheld (no bed count is printed). Exits include 18 deaths of which 12 confirmed, while Table 2 prints 5 intra-CTE confirmed deaths for Ituri. No carry-over is printed; SR185 ended at 383, and 383 + 95 - 81 = 397, not 394. Hot meals reached 359 of 372 patients, a denominator that differs from the census; both kept as printed.

Tshopo care prints 17 patients carried over (SR185 printed 18 at the end of the day, itself withheld), 6 admissions (1 confirmed, 5 suspects) and 5 exits (3 non-cases and 2 confirmed deaths), then 17 patients at the end of the day (5 confirmed and 12 suspects at two sites); 17 + 6 - 5 = 18. The 2 confirmed deaths are not in Table 2, which prints 0 Tshopo deaths for the day, and Table 1 prints 0 new Tshopo cases (a confirmed admission need not be a new case). The printed global occupancy of 42.5% with 50% and 25% at the two sites does not reconcile (16 patients at 50% and 1 at 25% give 32 + 4 = 36 beds and 47.2%). The Tshopo census, carry-over, occupancy and deaths are withheld.

Haut-Uele care prints 65 patients at the end of the day (36 confirmed, 29 suspects) with no carry-over, 11 admissions, 19 exits and 4 deaths. The census does not close against the SR185 end of day (65: 29 confirmed, 36 suspects), since 65 + 11 - 19 - 4 = 53; this is a cross-edition non-closure. The census and split are kept as printed and the SR185 figures are not changed. The 19 exits are said to bring the cumulative recoveries to 224, while the cover lists no Haut-Uele recoveries for the day; the exits are withheld. The printed 40% occupancy equals the SR185 rate although the split changed, and no bed count is printed, so it is kept only as the printed rate. The 11 admissions and the 4 deaths (which agree with Table 2) are kept.

Bas-Uele care prints 10 suspects carried over (SR185 printed 25 at the end of the day, itself withheld), 15 admissions and 17 non-case exits, then 25 suspects in isolation, the same figure as SR185; 10 + 15 - 17 = 8. The census and carry-over are withheld; the admissions and exits are kept as printed.

The census, carry-over and death are withheld; the beds and the start-of-day rate are kept as printed.

The census, carry-over and death are withheld; the beds and the start-of-day rate are kept as printed.

Sud-Ubangi care prints 3 suspects hospitalised (5% of 60 beds, 10% of 30 suspect beds) with 0 admissions and 0 exits that day, after 2 suspects at the end of SR185; Table 3 prints 4 Sud-Ubangi suspects transferred to CT/CTE and Table 5 prints 1 live validated alert at the control points with 100% transferred to CT/CTE, while the narrative does not report a transfer to CT/CTE. The census is kept as printed and no flow is derived.

Table 5 completeness: Ituri prints 95% for 60/62 (96.8%), the same ratio as SR185; the counts are kept and the percentage withheld. Nord-Kivu 20/21 and Sud-Kivu 5/9 repeat SR179 to SR185 and are withheld. Tshopo 18/18, Haut-Uele 11/13 and Sud-Ubangi 3/5 equal the SR184 cells (and Bas-Uele 17/22 the SR184 ratio, printed there as 72%), after 10/18, 9/13, ND and 19/22 in SR185; the page 6 narrative agrees with the Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele and Sud-Ubangi ratios (2, 5 and 2 sites not reporting) and all four are kept. The page 5 narrative prints 134/150 sites (89.3%), which equals the sum of the seven printed ratios including the two repeats, and is not promoted.

Table 5 rate cells: Ituri prints 100% of bodies swabbed or secured for the ratio 1/2 (50%); the percentage is withheld and the 2 bodies kept. Bas-Uele prints 100% of suspects transferred with 0 live validated alerts; nothing to measure, set to null. Printed 0% with nothing to measure is set to null: transferred and swabbed for Nord-Kivu (0 live validated, 0 bodies), all three rates for Sud-Kivu, Tshopo and Haut-Uele (0 alerts), and swabbed for Bas-Uele and Sud-Ubangi (0 bodies). Sud-Ubangi prints 100% of suspects transferred to CT/CTE for its 1 live validated alert, while the narrative does not report a transfer to CT/CTE and the Sud-Ubangi care paragraph prints 0 admissions that day; withheld. Nord-Kivu prints 0% investigated in 24h while the narrative reports its 1 alert invalidated after investigation; withheld.
Table 5 prints 77% of travellers sensitised for Bas-Uele while the page 6 narrative prints a low sensitisation rate of 78.4%; the Bas-Uele percentage is withheld.

The page 6 narrative states that the Sud-Ubangi figures (6 878 travellers) are a 3-day cumulative from 3 of 5 control points; the Sud-Ubangi traveller cell is withheld and left out of the national daily sum. The page 5 narrative total of 323 462 travellers includes it. The narrative also reports a +900 entry error in a Tshopo screening count, corrected from 315 038 to 314 138 screened nationally; whether the Tshopo 99% screening cell is before or after the correction is not stated, and 900 is about 4 points of the 22 322 Tshopo travellers, beyond the rounding of the cell; the table cannot settle it (the seven rounded screening cells give about 314 300 screened, within rounding of both national figures), so the Tshopo screening percentage is withheld. The national screened, handwashing and sensitised counts are not promoted.

Table 5 cumulative row: Ituri moves from 648 to 652 notified, 581 to 585 validated and 161 to 163 bodies, and Nord-Kivu from 416 to 417 notified, by exactly the daily cells; Sud-Kivu, Tshopo and Haut-Uele are unchanged with 0 alerts. Bas-Uele is unchanged at 196 notified, 25 validated and 10 bodies although 3 alerts are printed for the day. Sud-Ubangi prints a cumulative (6 notified, 6 validated) for the first time. The narrative cumulative (1 333 notified, 851 validated, 82 confirmed) equals the row sums, including the unchanged Bas-Uele cells. The cumulative alert counts are not promoted.

Safe-burial paragraphs do not close across editions: Nord-Kivu prints 78 alerts including 14 carried over, after 17 carried to the next day in SR185; Ituri prints 122 alerts including 21 carried over, after 14 carried in SR185, then 92 burials and 14 carried (106 of 122), and 85 of 107 bodies swabbed with 15 failures (100 of 107); Tshopo prints 14 death alerts (9 in morgues, 2 in health facilities, 3 at the CTE) with 1 complete burial and 3 carried over (4 against the 5 alerts outside morgues), and a morgue line of 9 admissions and 7 exits itemised as 8 + 1 admissions and 6 + 2 = 8 exits. The burial counts are not promoted.

The Nord-Kivu cumulative of 3 637 equals the SR185 3 352 plus the 285 vaccinated that day. Vaccination counts are not promoted.
The page 10 Nord-Ubangi CREC paragraph starts with a missing word and carries an editorial note (915 pupils printed as 505 girls and 440 boys, 945); CREC counts are not promoted.

Restated lines are not promoted as new SR186 events: the closure of one Nord-Kivu control point since September (SR185), the construction of two Sud-Ubangi control points with World Vision support (SR184 and SR185), the start of construction of a Tshopo isolation centre (SR185), 7 of 43 Ituri ambulances out of service (SR185), 130 of 632 Bas-Uele providers trained in IPC-WASH (SR185) and the Ituri PSEA awareness ratio of 15/36 zones (SR182).
Single-patient details in the PoE/PoC, laboratory, PCI, care, CREC, SMSPS and security paragraphs are not carried.

challenges.finding: Publisher reports, in Nord-Kivu, no household given a kit (0 of 7), a facility score card average of 53% with none of 7 facilities at 80% or more, 14 of 20 exposed staff assessed at high risk in Beni and 2 frontline workers among the confirmed cases in Butembo; in Ituri 13 patients without hot meals in Mandima and two inactive control points (insecurity, and a strike over two months of unpaid allowances); payment delays for providers in Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Haut-Uele and Bas-Uele, and community refusals fuelled by rumours; in Tshopo safe burials carried over for lack of teams, no food support for frontline workers at one transit centre, low Ebola training (10% to 33.3%) and no triage area in 5 assessed facilities, routine vaccination stopped by a strike of public facility health workers, 25 infected frontline workers of whom 9 investigated (36%), vaccination coverage lagging in Kabondo (48.2%) and Mangobo (73.7%) and second-round vaccination reporting at 16.7% (1 of 6 zones); in Haut-Uele no ring opened around the cases of the day, community reluctance to decontamination in Watsa and no functioning creche in affected zones; in Bas-Uele no patient in isolation receiving nutrition or psychosocial support for lack of deployed psychologists, 5 control points not reporting for lack of connectivity and mobility, and 121 remaining vaccine doses reported expired; in Nord-Ubangi 37 patients for 31 beds at the start of the day (119.4%), no permanent water point at the main hospital, a shortage of IPC inputs and no dedicated triage circuit. The Ituri ambulance line (7 of 43 out of service), the Bas-Uele IPC-WASH training line (130 of 632) and the closure of one Nord-Kivu control point repeat SR185 and are not counted here. No intervention effect is established.
